title: Code research, first pass: bots and custom-map details

facts.title: On several missions the single-player start key StartVehiclesGeneric holds a different container from the other 17 StartVehicles* slots
facts.fact: Single player reads StartVehiclesGeneric (1F13DE84). On most missions all 18 StartVehicles* slots hold the same container. On Mission_11a the generic slot is 123726 (Avatar Ingame Container, an on-foot pilot) while the other 17 slots are 124035 (Mad Dog). The pattern repeats in the data for other missions: M13b generic 123726 vs 17x Rommel 124052; M04 generic 124038 (Owens) vs 17x on-foot; M17a and M17b generic 124001 (Battle Armor) vs 17x NovaCat; M01b generic 125894 vs 17x 124486; M02 generic 125894 vs 17x 124001. The game starts the player on foot on M11a, as the grey pilot. Only the M11a start was seen in game; the other missions are from the data.
facts.how_to_use: Open: a copy of M13b or M04 played in game to confirm the on-foot start. An editor that shows the 17-slot container as the player start will report the wrong vehicle.

facts.title: On Mission_11a the intro cinema hands over from Foster Actor to the Uziels set at intro end
facts.fact: Mission_11a has two native swap sets, Swap Set Uziels (128588) and Swap Set Foster Actor (128587), both with bSwappedIn=1 at start. The trigger group TG - Intro End (under InGame Cinema 0 > Triggers) runs MAActionSwapSetOut on Foster Actor and MAActionSwapSetIn on Uziels, so the cinema stand-in is swapped out when the intro ends.
facts.how_to_use: Open: whether bSwappedIn=0 on a member set hides its members at load.

facts.title: Env_SnowDust_01 snow emitter sits in node 'efx', which maps local +Y to world -X, and uses the VD_Tank_Smoke texture
facts.fact: Env_SnowDust_01 is attached to node 'efx' of the precip model. That node's rotation maps local +Y to world -X and local Z to world Z; the mtb Offset (0,-20,10) matches the editor position (20,0,10) under this frame. Velocity is 18 m/s up the node's Y axis, with a 7 degree cone and an 8 x 9.9 x 50 box in node frame. The texture is VD_Tank_Smoke 64x64 (RGB mean 120, alpha mean 52/255); ENV_snow 256x256 is nearly empty (alpha mean 0.6), so the flakes change little. The M10 slope lift is about nine overlapping smoke quads.
facts.how_to_use: Open: whether the game also yaws the precipitation frame with the camera (untested; the M10 pose forward is near +Z).

facts.title: Translucent vegetation vertex light = Kd x (ambient + sun + sum of point-light colour x attenuation), with N.L = 1 on every term

subject.id: model vertex light V0 (translucent-shading models: trees, bushes, Env_Deadbush, grass)

facts.fact: For translucent-shading models (trees, bushes, Env_Deadbush, grass) the game's vertex light V0 is Kd x (ambient + sun + the sum of point-light colour x attenuation), with N.L = 1 for every term. M13a brush (Kd 2/3): d0 = 0.667(A+S) + p x lamp (0.36, 0.35, 0.28), with p between 0 and 0.72; unlit floor draws give A. M03 conifer (Kd 146): d0 = Kd(A+S) + lamp hue (1, 0.92, 0.53). This supersedes the earlier V0 = Kd x (A+S) reading and the rejected 0.86A + 1.29S fit.
facts.how_to_use: Open: whether the point-light term applies to other translucent classes (grass, Env_Deadbush on other maps).

facts.title: Game terrain program 08421 on M13a combines colour map, detail mix, vertex specular and light map as out = 4 x colormap x mix x (V1.rgb x V1.a x T3.a + T3.rgb)
facts.fact: Decoded from the combiner words of the M13a ground trace: s0 r1 = t1; s1 r0 = t0.a x t1 + (1 - t0.a) x t2 (mix); s2 r1 = 2 x r0 x c0.a (0.5), so mix; s3 r1 = 2 x mix x t0; s4 r0 = V1.rgb x T3.a; s5 r0 = r0 x V1.a + T3.rgb; s6 r0 = 2 x r0 x r1. Result: out = 4 x colormap x mix x (V1.rgb x V1.a x T3.a + T3.rgb). V1 is the vertex specular (d1) and T3 is the per-frame light map (file ambient x static lightmap + pools). The micro pass samples detail texture 80A28000 at x15.6 and x112 tiling.

facts.title: On M13a the editor's lit terrain term at the near ground (pixel 52,280) is 1.55x the game's, and the micro pass accounts for only 0.97 vs 0.85

subject.id: Mission_13a near-ground pixel (52,280) of the 640x480 same-pose shot

facts.fact: Same-pose stage dumps (editor on master 0c0ee4c, game trace m13a_ground_g3): lit terrain before micro, editor 20.9, 22.5, 19.5 vs game 13, 15, 13 (1.55x); after micro (final), editor 20.2, 22.0, 18.6 (x0.97) vs game 11, 12, 11 (x0.85). So most of the near-ground error sits in the lit terrain term, not in the micro pass. Light map lm.r 0.816 and lm.a 1.0 on the editor side; the game T3 texel was not dumped.
facts.how_to_use: Open: the game T3 (815EB000) texel at the pixel, to split the 1.55x between the light map and the vertex-specular term. Whole-image pair ratio (ground 1.4x near, 1.1x horizon) is in the same summary.

facts.title: MASpawner ParentID and SpawnID are 0 in every retail spawner; InitialID and InitialSecondID are odd/even 0xF80000xx pairs; the spawn tick does not test for a direct child
facts.fact: In the retail dumps (Mission_05, 7 spawners; Mission_04, 19; catalog over 1202 spawners) ParentID and SpawnID are always 0. The link to the stand object is the entity-tree parent (Mission_05 spawner 141817 sits under the NULL MACorporeal 32093), not these fields. At runtime the spawn handshake at 0x133C70 stores a value from [edi+0x2C] into the ParentID slot (runtime +0xA4), so ParentID becomes a spawned-unit slot (medium); what SpawnID (+0xA8) does is unknown. InitialID and InitialSecondID are a per-spawner pair in the 0xF80000xx range (InitialID odd: 0xF8000001, 03, 05; InitialSecondID the even partner), at runtime +0xAC and +0xB0. The spawn tick at 0x13321F gates only on the Enabled bit (runtime +0x78 bit 0x01), the handshake bit 0x10 and the caps/timer; no direct-child test was found. Enabled is 0 on 205 of 1202 retail spawners. Catalog offset + 0x20 = runtime offset.
facts.how_to_use: Open: what [edi+0x2C] is at 0x133C70; what SpawnID and the InitialID gate do; whether a spawner whose child is deleted still spawns (needs an in-game trace). Direct-child norm: 1201 child instances for 1202 spawners (class counts, not per spawner).

facts.title: The game shows ONE current objective (banner, HUD, radar, pause panel); the next appears only when the current one completes

subject.id: sub_0021D6F7 Objectives Display / global 0x4EB23C current objective index

facts.fact: Objective records live in a 30-record table (0x50E860, stride 0x64) read through one current index (global 0x4EB23C). The Objectives Display (sub_0021D6F7, vtable 0x48A4F0 slot 14) lists record i only when i == the current index; HUD_Text (sub_001FC461) shows the current record's text when it is enabled, not done and non-empty; the start banner (sub at 0x1F7D9D) and radar target markers (sub at 0x21DA39) also read the current record. Completion (sub_00169A49) marks every record whose mission variables are all set as done, but the index advances (sub_001699ED: next record not yet done) ONLY when the completed record is the current one; a later objective finished early is ticked silently and skipped. Retail missions are linear chains of 5-16 enabled slots (M02, M03: 'Intro Over' -> 'Steal Tank' -> 'Kill Stuff' -> .), never parallel lists. Proven in game on an editor-built mission (g3, d12_objective_order.ma2map): the start banner listed only 'FIRST: wait 8 seconds'; after its 8 s timer the pause panel listed only 'SECOND: survive 5 minutes'. A disabled (ObjectiveEnabledBool 0) current record shows nothing and stalls the advance (inferred from the walk, not observed). Editor: the Objectives section shows a hint saying the game shows one objective at a time.
facts.how_to_use: Editor tab: Objectives & Triggers > Add objective. Author objectives as an ordered chain; all user lines need EnabledBool 1 and a text. Do not expect objectives 2-3 in the pause list until 1 is done. Unknown: the start-banner and pause-panel builders themselves, the sub_00165164==0x10 / obj+0x69 branch of sub_0021D6F7.

facts.title: Water wading is the type-map bit (8) plus MAEnvironment per-type values; no drown/swim code found; retail shallow water is ~0.3-1.6 m deep, editor default dig capped at 1.4 m

subject.id: type map cell bit 8 (shallow wade) / MAWater plane / MAEnvironment per-type water values

facts.fact: The game decides wading from the terrain type-map bit (8 shallow, 16 deep, 32 waterway) and MAEnvironment per-type values (Speed, Damage, Cooling, Mech may enter, Pilot in for shallow/deep/waterway); no code was found that drowns, slows or pushes out a pilot by water depth, and no swim state exists: the pilot follows the terrain bed. Retail data (all worlds with MAWater): type-8 cells lie median 0.3-1.2 m, p90 <=1.6 m below the plane (Bogged Down 0.9/1.2, flat MP lakes No Man's Land 2.9 m, Troubled Waters 4.4 m); type-16 cells 2-8 m (campaign only). The old editor default lake (min(pond_depth, 0.3 x short side)) was ~8 m with every cell below the surface marked 8, and an on-foot pilot sank fully. Editor fix: dug basin default capped at 1.4 m (kWadeDepth, water_ux.cpp dig_water_basin) with a 'Deep (only 'Mechs can wade)' tick for up to 8 m; Place water marks playable cells under the footprint as water ground (type map 8; moving/deleting water now clears old marks, 27ff6ab). GAME PROOF (g3, PC Release, UI-made wade_shallow.ma2map, default dig): the pilot wades thigh-deep, head and torso above the surface, no sinking. Deep (type 16): game-observed g3: a lake ~4 m deep with cells marked 16 lets the on-foot pilot walk in fully submerged and out the far side, no block, no damage in ~10 s (default MAEnvironment); a 1.2 m lake marked 8 is knee-deep. Editor now marks under-water cells deeper than 1.6 m as 16 ('Deep water' overlay) and warns that a pilot ends up below the surface. Shallow water reads faint from afar (thickness alpha ~ vertical depth/4, MEDIUM).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: Terrain > Water > Place water / Dig a basin. Keep wadable lakes 1-2 m deep; use the Deep tick only for mechs.

facts.title: Player death restarts the mission by itself; retail missions have no lose-on-player-death trigger, and an empty Destroyed(IncludePlayers) trigger fires at load
facts.fact: Runtime-observed: when the player dies the game restarts the level itself; a lost custom mission (Lose action, e.g. the Countdown template reaching 00:00) also silently restarts with no 'Mission failed' screen in Custom Scenarios. Retail missions have no trigger watching the player for this. Where retail does use MATriggerDestroyed with IncludePlayers 1 ('TD - PlayerDead' 261413, 'TD - Player Died' 155977/'TD - Player Is Dead' 156618) it carries a DestroySet (MoeEntitySet) + CombineMethod 1 + TypeOfCheck 2; the set is what makes it wait. An editor trigger with IncludePlayers 1 and NO set/units passes at once: Lose fires at load and the mission reloads forever; the 'Lose if the player is destroyed' template was removed and Check scenario flags the pattern as Must fix. Members of sets 261412/130400 are not in the dictionary (LOW). Engine death path (failed.ggf, sub_001FB241, health test sub_000C8BDC) has no caller found: general case LOW.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: Objectives & Triggers > Templates; Check scenario. No lose-on-death trigger is needed. Use the Countdown template for lose conditions.

facts.title: A 0 s timer that starts a cinema did not play the intro in an editor-built mission; 1 s and 3 s do (retail Mission_05 uses 0 s)
facts.fact: An earlier 3 s timer cinema also played (G6). The editor wiring is field-identical to retail Mission_05 'TT - StartUp' (a 0 s timer), so the wiring is not the cause. Code (HIGH): the timer's first update only ARMS it (sets +0xBC armed and +0xB4 start time from the game clock at 0x4E2440); it fires on the next update when elapsed >= +0xB8, so a 0 s timer fires one tick after arming, not on the arming frame. MAActionActivateCinema returns silently if its cinema uid resolves to null; the cinema start sub_00155A99 is a no-op if a cinema is already active (byte 0x4EB19C set) and starts no controller when the Camera Controllers child list is empty. Best explanation (MEDIUM, not reproduced): the 0 s fire lands in the first ticks while load state is still settling or another cinema is active, Start returns silently and the fire is consumed; 1 s and 3 s let those frames pass. No 'mission started' gate on trigger updates was found. How retail Mission_05 avoids it is unknown (LOW). Editor: 'Play at mission start' and the 'Play the intro cutscene when the mission starts' template now write a 1 s timer.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: Objectives & Triggers > Templates > Play the intro cutscene when the mission starts; Cameras & Cutscenes > Play at mission start. Keep intro cinema timers at 1 s or more and start only one cinema at mission begin. Open: trace 0x4EB19C and the trigger tick at the 0 s fire; check TrgTimerDuration units (minutes vs seconds) and the 0x4E2438 vs 0x4E2440 clocks.

MP uses 404 trigger/action/event instances (campaign 2647), from only these classes (MP instances / MP worlds): MATriggerTimer 43/16, MATriggerDestroyed 60/9, MATriggerRadius 20/5, MATriggerMenuActivate 30/6, MATriggerGameTime 16/16, MATriggerNationRadius 4/1, MAActionSound 72/16, MAActionAI 45/5, MAActionAttribute 34/16, MAActionCheckItGoal 30/6, MAActionMusic 16/16, MAActionNation 24/12, MAActionRemoveEntity 5/5, MAActionResponse 1/1, MAActionTeleport 4/1. facts.title: MAEnvironment deep-water fields (SpeedDeep, DamageDeep, CoolingDeep, MechDeep, PilotDeep): retail value spread, no consumer found; default deep water did not hurt or block a pilot

subject.id: MAEnvironment deep/shallow/waterway fields (reader sub_00124CC1, entity = reader offset + 0x20)

facts.fact: MAEnvironment carries one group of five fields per water type, selected by the terrain type-map bit (8 shallow, 16 deep, 32 waterway): Speed ('Speed in - deep water'), Damage, Cooling, Mech ('Mech may enter') and Pilot ('Pilot in'): SpeedDeep, DamageDeep, CoolingDeep, MechDeep, PilotDeep (names from reader sub_00124CC1; reader offsets known only for CoolingWaterway +0x1C0, DamageLava +0x1F0, SpeedShallow +0x23C, entity = reader + 0x20). No code consumer was found for any deep field, so what the deep values do is INFERRED, not code-confirmed. Retail spread over the 66 worlds with a MAEnvironment (value x worlds). DEEP: Speed 100x49, 75x8, 90x6, 50x3; Damage 0x50, 200x8, 125x3, 0.1x2; Cooling 0x44, 16x14, 8x5, 4x2; Mech may enter 1x57, 0x9; Pilot in 1x51, 100x11, 0x3, 10x1. SHALLOW: Speed 100x52, 90x8, 75x3, 95x3; Damage 0x55, 100x7, 10x3, 200x1; Cooling 0x39, 8x21, 16x3, 4x3; Mech 1x54, 0x12; Pilot 1x54, 100x7, 0x4, 2x1. WATERWAY: Speed 100x63, 90x3; Damage 0x65, 1x1; Cooling 0x52, 4x11, 8x3; Mech 1x55, 0x11; Pilot 1x56, 0x10. 'Pilot in' is bimodal (1.0 vs 100.0); the scale (flag vs percent) is unconfirmed. Game-observed (g3, wade_deep.ma2map, default MAEnvironment): an on-foot pilot walks fully submerged through a ~4 m lake of type-16 cells, no block and no damage in ~10 s, consistent with the default/most common DamageDeep 0 and PilotDeep 1; this does NOT support the editor tooltip claim that deep water is 'Mechs only' (mech behaviour and the retail DamageDeep 200/125 worlds untested). Open: the sampler that reads the type-map bit and indexes these fields (the AI singleton reads CoolingWaterway; sub_001234D6 reads env+0x1C0, attribution may be wrong), whether MechDeep 0 blocks a mech, whether Damage is per second.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: Environment > Water values / Terrain > Water 'Deep' tick.

facts.title: Retail developers prefix trigger names with a short code (TT, TD, TR, TG, TL, TB, TMA, TA, TC, TPVT, TGT, TUB, TNR, TSB) that maps almost 1:1 to the trigger class

subject.id: retail trigger/action instance names, 11,518 named instances over 60 worlds

facts.fact: Parsed from all 60 world WDFs (11,518 named MATrigger*, MAAction*, MAGroup, MoeEntitySet, instances). Code -> class (consistency): TT = MATriggerTimer (861/884, 97%; 'TT - Start', 'TT - StartUp'); TD = MATriggerDestroyed (451/451, 100%; 'TD - PlayerDead'); TR = MATriggerRadius (388/388, 100%; 'TR - Inside HUB'); TG = base MATrigger (370/387, 96%; 'TG - Intro End', 'TG - 2 start': trigger group / generic); TL = MATriggerLogic (297/297; 'TL - All enemies dead'); TB = MATriggerCuboidalVolume (121/122; box inferred); TMA = MATriggerMenuActivate (73/75; 'TMA - gate switch'); TA = MATriggerAttach (35/35); TC = MATriggerCounter (32/37; 'Counter - ' for 5 others); TPVT = MATriggerPlayerVehicleType (22/23); TGT = MATriggerGameTime (16/16; 'TGT - GameOver'); TUB = MATriggerUber (7/7); TNR = MATriggerNationRadius (4/4); TSB = MATriggerSpider (2/2). All MAAction* names start with 'Action - ' which is a class label, not a code (4,532 instances, 100%). MAGroup, MoeEntitySet, MAWaypointGroup, MASwapSet names are ordinary text (no codes). Exceptions: 23 MATriggerTimer names have no code, about 12 MATrigger names are default 'Trigger (Generic)_00006', separators vary ('TT-delay', 'TD -ship', 'TT_delay', 'TR Player in Uziel'), casing varies ('Intro end'/'Intro End'). Action names quote trigger names verbatim ('Action - Enable TT - delay stiletto intro'), so renaming a trigger would break such action text. The codes are developer convention; whether runtime code reads them is unchecked. Editor display rule: strip with a whitelist regex ^(TT|TD|TR|TG|TL|TB|TMA|TA|TC|TPVT|TGT|TUB|TNR|TSB)(\s*[-_]\s*|\s+) (case-insensitive) for trigger classes and ^Action\s*-\s* for MAAction*; do NOT use a generic [A-Z]{1,4} pattern.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: Triggers list/tab display names (prefix stripping) and new-trigger default names; keep the stored name unchanged.

facts.title: The mission-variable table (0x4EB9E0) is read by the objective check AND by every MATrigger fire gate and MATriggerTimer, so deleting an objective's variable setter can break triggers
facts.fact: Readers (code-confirmed by a literal grep of 0x4EB9E0 over recomp_*.c): the objective completion check sub_00169A49 (recomp_0037.c:15436-15520; a record is done when every variable id at record +0x2C has a nonzero byte); the MATrigger base fire routine sub_001452D4 (recomp_0032.c:18049, read at 0x1453C3 /:18234), which takes a variable id from MATrigger+0x90 and fires only when table[id] == byte MATrigger+0x94 (ids <= 0 or >= 30 skip the check); MATriggerTimer sub_00148BB7 (recomp_0033.c:3971, read at:4031); and the save path sub_000F175D (recomp_0024.c:21776). Writers: MAActionMissionVariableSet sub_001A94A1 (recomp_0045.c:37), sub_0016990A (recomp_0037.c:15201), load sub_000F235C (recomp_0024.c:23326). No direct reads found in MATriggerLogic, MAActionGameCondition, MATriggerDestroyed or MATriggerRadius (literal grep only; indirect reads through a call to sub_001452D4 are not excluded, and the older claim that MATriggerRadius sub_00145D77 reads the table is not supported). Retail catalog: MissionVariable range -1.29, 2751 instances (~line 48821; the sample is -1 in most, 0 in a few), so non-negative ids DO appear on retail triggers. Not checked: whether a retail trigger's MissionVariable id equals an objective's ob<N>var<j> in a given mission (no per-object MATrigger dump for Mission_05).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: when an objective is deleted, keep the setter action's variable (just unlink the objective) instead of writing -1, unless the variable is proven unused by every trigger in the level: a trigger gated on that variable would otherwise never fire (or always fire).

facts.title: An on-foot pilot completes a 'Destroy these' objective (4 demolition charges kill a Loki) and wins the mission; the objective check has no killer or weapon test
facts.fact: Game-observed: new flat mission, player start On foot (pilot), one enemy Loki ~50 m ahead with AI off, Objectives > Add objective > Destroy these (the Loki), 'Win the mission when every objective is done' ticked. The pilot's fire key drops demolition charges; 4 charges destroyed the Loki, the objective completed and the mission was WON (return to hub). This matches the code read: the objective check sub_00169A49 (recomp_0037.c:15436-15520) tests only mission-variable bytes and never the killer or weapon. It also proves in game the full chain Destroy objective -> objective complete -> Win (reinforcement arrival remains unproven). The on-foot kill is slow, not impossible.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: Objectives & Triggers > Add objective > Destroy these. The on-foot start only needs a hint about how slow the kill is, not a block.

facts.title: MABarrel.BarrelChargeEffectID 318 = MAEffect 'PPC L3 Charge' is the charge effect shared by most mech guns; Hammer, LRM, SRM and mortars have none
facts.fact: Retail data: BarrelChargeEffectID 318 = MAEffect 'PPC L3 Charge' is shared by Laser, Pulse Laser, Machine Gun, Autocannon, Gauss, Flamer and the Elemental/BattleArmor lasers; PPCs use their own (26265 L1, 697 L2, 318 L3); AlphaStrike uses 125299; Hammer, LRM, SRM, Guided Missile and mortars have 0 (no charge effect). So a mech charging any of the 318 guns shows the blue PPC-style arcs (retail behaviour, not an editor error). Hammer is BarrelClass 14 like LRM: a hold-to-charge lob missile (BarrelChargeRate 75, TimeToMaxLob 2.0, no lock). Loki loadout 32717 = SRM + Autocannon x2 + Pulse Laser.
facts.how_to_use: Editor: weapon/loadout display; no editor control changes this. When a render or effect audit sees PPC-style arcs on a laser/autocannon mech, it is the shared 318 effect.

facts.title: Bowman Hammer makes no sound request while charging and one fire-cue request per release; silent charge is retail behaviour
facts.fact: Game-confirmed: holding the Bowman Hammer produces NO sound request during the charge and exactly one fire-cue request per release (chain 000D34C5 / 000D06BC / 0008252B).
facts.how_to_use: Audio/weapon audits: do not report 'no charge sound' for the Hammer as a bug.

facts.title: Bot vehicle preference in the code: every 'Mech = 1.0, VTOL 0.55 + 0.05 x skill, BattleArmor 0.30 + 0.05 x skill; the game's m_nBattleScore is unused
facts.fact: Corrects bots-vehicle-value (which says tank 0.75, BA 0.70 + 0.08 x skill, VTOL 0.45 + 0.08 x skill). Current code: vehicle_pref(MECH) = 1.0 for every 'Mech, VTOL = 0.55 + 0.05 x skill, BattleArmor = 0.30 + 0.05 x skill (ma2_bot_brain.c:1096-1106, 1187, pick_swap 1240); the skill bonus makes Elites prefer VTOL/BA. The game's own strength rating m_nBattleScore (Templates.mgf, getter vtable +0x90, loader 0x464BEC) is not used: light 'Mechs 6 (Puma, Uller, Raven, Cougar, Kit Fox, Owens, Hackman, Corvus), 7 (Belial, Mad Dog, Stiletto, Raptor), 9 (Loki, MadCat, Bowman, Thor, Catapult, Hellbringer, Summoner, Timber Wolf, NovaCat), 10 (Atlas, Ragnarok, Star Adder, Prometheus, Blood Asp); Rommel/APC 4; VTOL - Player 4; BattleArmor/Elemental 3; PlayerTurret Gauss / Guided Missile 2; pilots 1. So a bot takes the nearest free 'Mech, not the strongest.
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3B-01 (proposed pref = 0.7 + 0.03 x score). Use m_nBattleScore as the game's own vehicle strength.

facts.title: Bots no longer eject at low HP; a vehicle destroyed with its pilot inside kills the pilot (the bot respawns as a full-HP pilot at base)
facts.fact: Corrects bots-eject-rule ('eject below 12 % HP with an enemy within 80 m'): that rule is no longer in the bot code. Current exits: swap (HP <= 35 % AND a usable vehicle <= 70 m AND no enemy within 50 m), trapped/bail, and not-allowed kinds (ma2_bot_brain.c:1240-1270, 1660-1672). Runtime data (31 runs): 216 of 277 vehicle -> pilot transitions happen at hp < 0.15 (mech 115, VTOL 51, BA 28, tank 22) and the 'pilot' reappears at its base with hp 1.0 (E2E_1022 bot 10: MECH hp 0.00 at 724,1306 for 3 s, then PILOT at 955,827 = a respawn). In MP a vehicle destroyed with the pilot inside = the pilot dies; there is no automatic eject on destruction. Bots therefore ride every vehicle to its death.
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3B-02 (mode-gated bail-out proposed). Do not assume bots eject.

facts.title: The bot stuck watchdog fires after 6 s without 3 m of progress (2.5 s on a boarding leg), not the design's 2 s, and recovers in several escalating steps
facts.fact: Code read: stuck = no 3 m progress in 6 s (2.5 s on a boarding leg) or 12 s 'shuttling' inside an 11 m patch; recovery: the spot 4 m ahead becomes a per-bot obstacle (90 s), ma2_trav_learn 30 s, re-probe + wall sweep; a second stall on open map adds a shared 'unseen obstacle' (r 2.5 m, kept for the whole match, side_prop_add ctrl.c ~1418); then backtrack 4 s to a breadcrumb; jet hop on 'Mech/BA; status.trapped after 4 stalls makes the brain bail out (eject, no_board 120 s). section 6 says ~2 s. Log lines ([BOT-DROP], [BOT-CTRL] no progress/shuttling, [BOT-BACKTRACK], [BOT-ESCAPE], [BOT-TRAPPED], [BOT-NAV] learned) print only with RECOMP_BOT_DIAG and [BOT-SUM] has no stuck counters.
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3A-01/t3A-05/t3A-06. Quote 6 s, not 2 s.

facts.title: The bot planner links ledges DOWN only (one-way drops, <= 20 m); there are no jet-up links, so 'Mechs/BA never jet onto a ridge unless stuck
facts.fact: Code read: ma2_bot_path.c:176-190 and 355-385 build one-way DROP links down (<= 20 m reach, forbidden for 10 min per 15 m edge after a failed attempt); going up a ledge is never planned: jets up only as stuck recovery (ctrl.c ~1439) or a brain-picked roof (upjet). Design section 6 promises 'Mech/BA jump links. Also: moving vehicles are excluded from the static obstacle grid (obstacle_top: movers -> dyn) and handled as dynamic obstacles with path invalidation. Battle Armor causes 206 of 324 no-progress stalls in the 20-run s13 sweep (Go Commando 41 + 49, Rush Hour 59, In Your Face FFA 20), mostly single stalls in open ground; BA minimum carrot is 8 m (ctrl.c ~81, kind_min_carrot), inside MoveTo's known 5-10 m halt band (inferred cause). Confirmed on the current build (3D's Killing Field run): 76 of 80 stalls are Battle Armor, all single stalls, 80 backtracks.
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3A-03/t3A-04.

facts.title: The bot nav graph is chosen by the loading archive, so a custom editor map built on one of 4 graph-shipping bases would load the base level's graph
facts.fact: Code + log: the graph source is picked from the loading ARCHIVE; a custom editor map reports its BASE level (3D's 6v6 log: '[BOT-NAV] map=boggeddown.mgf shipped=none', source=generated). Four bases ship a 'Mech graph: In Your Face, New River City, Rush Hour (= Mission16_Mech.map), Witch Cauldron (ma2_bot_mapid.c:28-43); the others generate from the obstacle grid (Killing Field 7947 nodes / 407 components; Over Falls 7381 / 513; Go Commando 2036 / 116). A custom map built on one of the four would load the RETAIL graph for edited terrain (roam points brain.c ~1080, flank via-points ~1021); the editor-written Pathfinding/Scn<ID>_Mech.map is never used. The bots find every other map feature by CLASS at run time, not by name or retail UID: vehicles = MAMech/MATank/MAFlyer/MATurret + entry zones from their MACrateGenerator children; helipads = any MABuilding with an MACollectionArea child; power-ups = MAPowerUp; CTF flags = MAFlagCTF + MATriggerFlagStatus; data cores = MASnatchItDataCore; checkpoints = MACheckpoint / MATriggerCheckpoint; water = MAWater; 'home' = the bot's first spawn spot (b->home_pos, brain.c:2485). No teleport/jump-pad logic exists. Missing features degrade gracefully (no vehicle: fight on foot; no pad: VTOL uses an armour power-up within 300 m; no objectives: deathmatch behaviour).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: MP map authoring; bots audit t3A-08, t3-custom-00.05.

facts.title: Bots navigate custom terrain: the walking planner always runs on an obstacle grid built from the live terrain; the coarse 20 m node graph is generated unless the base level ships a 'Mech graph
facts.fact: Code + logs: (1) the walking planner (ma2_bot_path.c, 2 m grid A*) ALWAYS runs on an obstacle grid built at match start from the live terrain + colliders (core.c ensure_nav -> ma2_trav_build, then a fine prop pass), on retail and custom maps alike; this is what bots actually walk. (2) The coarse 20 m node graph (roam points, flank via-points, connectivity) is generated from that grid on any map whose base ships no 'Mech graph (3D's custom 6v6: '[BOT-NAV] obstacle grid ok 508x508 . source=generated:gen_B670C477 nodes=2601 components 1'). An unknown cache id -> terrain-match against the 4 shipped graphs, accepted only at score >= 0.5 and 0.2 ahead of the next; else generated and cached as %LOCALAPPDATA%\MechAssault2\BotNav\gen_<terrain fingerprint>.map (edited terrain = new fingerprint; with the obstacle grid ready the cache is skipped and the graph regenerated each match). Only the 4 bases that ship a graph (In Your Face, New River City, Rush Hour, Witch Cauldron) give a custom map the RETAIL graph (bots3-nav-graph-chosen-by-loading-archive-.). The bot source has ONE real retail tie (the archive pick in ma2_bot_mapid.c: 14 MP archives + core.c k_nav_archives); everything else is map-agnostic (no retail UIDs, template ids, coordinates or names used as code). The optional stuck-memory file (off by default) is keyed by the archive name, so custom maps on one base would share penalties (t3-custom-A06).
facts.how_to_use: Editor: MP map authoring; bots audit t3A-08, t3-custom-A01.A06.

facts.title: Bot lanes are planned from the live terrain at t >= 1 s in team modes only (up to 3 lanes, none in FFA or when the bases are < 300 m apart)
facts.fact: Code read: in TEAM modes at t >= 1 s the core plans team-centroid -> enemy-centroid on the obstacle grid, adds a danger corridor along it and re-plans twice, giving up to 3 distinct lanes ([BOT-LANES]); each bot takes one (g_lane, lane_pick / lane_point; flank via-points must be reachable on the node graph). Not built when the bases are < 300 m apart or in FFA modes (bots go straight and rely on roam/flank). Test map c3-proof\bots_custom_full.ma2map (id 0DAA6085) was rebuilt with two steep Plateau walls giving north hills / central valley with a building choke / south lake + bridge to measure per-lane traversal. GAME PROOF: [BOT-LANES] found exactly the 3 lanes built in the editor ('3 lane(s) from 156,509 to 869,507 (corridor 128 m) in 15 ms'; main = central valley, side +1 apex 498,332 = south lake/bridge, side -1 apex 668,662 = north hills); bots were handed lanes; traffic in x 400-650 by z band: central 252 samples (7 bots), south 57 (2), north 52 (2), 0 on the walls, so every lane is used (central-heavy: it holds the objective and is shortest). Only 5 no-progress stalls in the match; one pilot wedged 30 s at 181,291 by its own base. Lane use detail (t3-custom-path-D01): most bots stay in one lane all match (bots 5/6/8 central only, 9 south only, 7 north only, 10 used north+south); no wall jumps, 2 % of samples clumped (< 8 m), no bot stuck 20 s+ in one 3 m cell; retail-flat comparison td6v6 (no lanes): 25 % clumped, all in the centre. Retail comparison (t3-custom-path-A06, 3D's Killing Field copy TD 6v6, killingfield_td.log): '[BOT-LANES] 3 lane(s) from 387,1667 to 1112,921 (corridor 187 m)', side lanes 408 m and 301 m off the main route, graph generated from the obstacle grid (map=killingfield.mgf shipped=none, 7947 nodes), so custom terrain fans out like retail. Stuck counts there: 80 stalls (76 Battle Armor), 0 trapped, 3 learned obstacles, 2 escapes; the t3A-02 ledge-drop retry did not recur (BA start, 0 drops; needs a 'Mech-start run).
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3-custom-path-A02/A03; use bots_custom_full for lane counts.

facts.title: A damaged VTOL repairs at an armour pack within 300 m or the nearest pad within 2.5 km, else fights on; a mode with missing flags/bases/cores scores no objective and plays as deathmatch
facts.fact: Code read: helipads = any MABuilding with an MACollectionArea child (core.c ~2363, ma2_bot_pad_add); the editor palette's 'Military VTOL pad' carries one (bots_custom_full: 6 collection areas). A damaged VTOL (hp < 20-45 % by skill) heads for an armour pack within 300 m (no enemy within 120 m of it), else the nearest pad within 2.5 km; with NEITHER, G_REPAIR is never scored and it fights on until it dies (no fly-home-and-hover path); ground units do not use pads at all. objective_eval scores objectives only when w->nobjectives > 0 and obj_find returns both sides' pieces (brain_obj.c ~47-57, 71-76, 269-283): CTF without flags or Snatch It without bases/cores gives objective score 0 and the bots fight as in Team Destruction (no freeze, no wandering). The editor flags these as Must fix ('[text omitted]', 'Snatch It needs the Snatch It bases / data core', verified on bots_custom_stripped, id 1C6565DE). The game does not require a helipad or heal pad at a base, so a missing pad is not a Must fix (suggested Check warning only).

facts.title: A BattleArmor swapping into a 'Mech does not reserve it (claims exist only for GET_VEHICLE), so most BA bots chase the same free 'Mechs at every BA-start match
facts.fact: Log + code: claims are made only for MA2_ORD_GET_VEHICLE, and order_swap drives with travel/eject orders, so several BattleArmors chase the same free 'Mech; the first in takes it, the rest find it occupied, re-pick and set off again. ctf.log: 641 swap-go + 101 swap-eject notes; 7 of 11 BA bots start a swap at t = 1.2 and are still BattleArmor at t = 31 (again at 33 and 63); only 9 swaps complete in 180 s; snatch.log similar (16 stuck episodes, 6 swaps). Observed, root cause read from code (inferred). MORE EVIDENCE: goal=swap is 507 of ~2000 samples in CTF and 434 in Snatch It; on a retail-terrain map (Killing Field copy, Battle Armor start, TD 6v6, bots-t3d\killingfield_td.log) goal=swap is 1013-1110 of ~1900 bot samples (53-58 %), 8 of 11 BA bots start a swap at t = 1.1 and are still BattleArmor at t = 31, 2-4 bots chase the SAME 'Mech (02451C40) in every 5 s window for the first minute, only 8 boardings and 13 kills in 170 s. On foot, bots also dither between vehicles (t3-custom-D02: bot 2 set getveh on 4 different vehicles without boarding any; 170 getveh samples, 1 boarding). FIX PROOF: C3 smokes PASSED, no crash. Counters '[C7] c3': custom_full TD assigned = 16, reassigned = 1, switches = 14, foot_getveh = 4; Killing Field TD assigned = 30, swaps_claimed = 19, swap_cooldown_blocks = 11, commit_holds = 3, and goal=swap fell to 33 % of samples against the 51 % baseline. So claiming swap targets plus a per-bot swap cooldown and vehicle-target commitment cut the swap churn by about a third on the retail-terrain map (single runs, not a large sample).
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3B-08 (make the swap target a claim); explains t3D-05 churn.

facts.title: On an editor-made map with vehicle pads only, Team Destruction had no vehicle entity at run time (CTF copy did), and pilots stalled 5-12 m short of an editor-placed 'Mech
facts.fact: Run logs: on t3d_allmodes (pads: BattleArmor, Loki, Guided-Missile turret; no parked vehicles; players start on foot) Team Destruction had NO vehicle entity at run time (0 [BOT-HULL], 0 [BOT-VEHPICK], all 11 bots pilots for 180 s) while CTF on the BattleArmor-start copy had 'Mechs, VTOLs and turrets (46 [BOT-HULL]): the pads did not produce vehicles for Team Destruction, most likely because pads or their vehicles sit only in the CTF/BaseWar/Snatch game-type groups of the editor kit, or a pad only spawns when asked (inferred; matches the wiki rule that match logic and spawners live in MAMissionTypeGroup per game type). On the editor map bots_custom_full pilots reach the editor-placed 'Mech but stall 5-12 m from its hull without tapping Y, then silently drop it (custfull_td.log: 4 of 5 arrivals stalled, e.g. bot 0 frozen at 232.38,620.36 for 2 s, 5.7 m from hull 018A9020, dest = entry 241,624 behind it); retail runs never do this (574/574 boarded). Possible editor pad stand height / collision difference (inferred). UPDATE: on the stripped test map bots_custom_stripped (every MAPowerUp/MAPowerupDrop deleted, incl. ones nested in spawners / mission-type groups) in Team Destruction all 11 bots stayed pilots for 164 s: the 4 'Mechs EXIST (BOT-HULL kind=2 at 225,378 / 791,404 / 236,616 / 743,285) but none is usable (0 'Mech picks vs 11 in custfull2_td); the same 'Mechs were picked in custstrip_ctf. Cause is MAP DATA, not a bot fault: bot-side 'usable' needs an ARMED entry zone (see bots3-vehicle-usable-needs-armed-entry-zone.), and the strip evidently removed what arms the TD pads' entry zones. Proposed A/B (3D): RECOMP_TEST_DUMP_NEAR=791,404,15,5 on custstrip_td vs custfull2_td should list the 'Mech's children (expect MACrateGenerator + MATriggerPoint in full, missing/unarmed in stripped). Editor implication: deleting powerups/salvage must not touch pad internals; Check should warn 'This vehicle pad cannot be boarded: its entry zone has no crate generator/trigger point' (players hit the same dead pad). ROOT CAUSE FOUND: the editor copied a game type's retail objects only for some types; Team Destruction's vehicle bays and turrets sit in a retail group called 'TD Specific' that was never copied, so TD maps had no vehicles. 9982d3c makes EVERY ticked game type copy its retail objects on New / tick. Editor proof (MCP l3d): New map TD + Check It -> status 'Added the Team Destruction, Check It objects', TD bay groups present (f13_new_dialog.png); game proof pending on g3 (CheckIt + TD 5v6 on that map). This resolves the earlier 'pads sit in per-game-type groups' inference.
facts.how_to_use: Editor MP authoring: check which MAMissionTypeGroup the pad belongs to; bots audit t3-custom-06/07.

facts.title: Destruction (type 10) is a free-for-all; team game types are 1-3 and 0xB-0x11 (correction of the k_modes 'team_type 1-3 and 0xA-0x11')
facts.fact: CORRECTION: team_type is (gt > 0 && gt <= 3) (gt > 0xA && gt <= 0x11), so Destruction (0xA = 10) is FFA, NOT a team mode; the t04_scenario k_modes fact ('team_type is true for 1-3 and 0xA-0x11') is stale and the t01b table is right. Game-proven: bots-t3d\destruction.log shows all bots on team 0 (103 kills in 115 s). LMS (type 9) is a real FFA with one life each (11 players, 'Talon Wins!' after 44 s, lms_end.png). Other modes run once each on g3 (all 10 editor-offered autostart modes): Not-It 'It' passed 19 times in 150 s with all non-It bots chasing It (229 kills); Snatch It: red bots carried 2 cores into their base, cores grabbed 6 times, 56 kills; Team LMS ended ~40 s; Team Destruction in Battle Armor 137 kills (Blue 360-51). The engine has 17 game types (2 Soccer, 5 GiantKillers, 7 ScoutMatch, 8 SkirmishMatch, 11 TeamScoutMatch, 12 TeamSkirmishMatch, 13 TakeIt besides the 10 known); scenario autostart k_modes (ma2_scenario.c:1001-1005) and the bot code know only 10, so selectable extras would play as deathmatch. Test-harness bug: autostart compares --mode with the map's own mode names (ma2_scenario.c:1068), so the aliases 'LMS' / 'TeamLMS' never match and fall back to the map's first mode ('[SCENARIO] test autostart: mode LMS is not one of C6DC280C's modes, using TeamDestruction').

facts.title: On editor-made maps Check It and Base War matches end ~5 s after the start, and Grinder is an empty field (no waves, no vehicles)

subject.id: bots-t3d checkit.log / basewar.log / grinder.log (g3, editor maps)

facts.fact: Game-proven: (1) Check It ticked on an editor map adds NO checkpoints (MACheckpoint; CTF/Base War/Snatch It get kits, the editor status after Create lists only those); with no checkpoints the match ENDS AT ONCE: 'Red Team Wins!' 0-0 about 5 s in (bot lines stop at t = 5, 0 [OBJ-CLAIM]). (every blue player 1 point, 0 kills, 0 deaths); both sides got two kit buildings (24000 hp and 2000 hp, nation 1 and 2) from the editor's Base War kit; the cause is UNKNOWN (what the game's Base War win check reads: a base/generator link or count the kit misses for the red side); not separated from kit-vs-game yet (needs a retail Base War map re-test). Time-to-first-'Mech in Grinder is therefore still unmeasured (wiki bots-grinder-ba-swap ~15 s). facts.title: Bots hold every free 'Mech while the human is on foot (measured: 33 of 41 samples); bots have no knowledge of the human's intent and no last-'Mech reservation

subject.id: ma2_bot_brain.c vehicle_usable 1174-1183, 1196-1203, pick 1222-1238, pick_swap 1240-1270; ma2_bots_core.c claims 2796-2806

facts.fact: The 'race' case (a bot boards the 'Mech the human runs to) cannot yet be measured: in MCP runs the human never moves and the only human-walk hook RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_BOARD walks to a VTOL (ma2_bots_core.c:3734-3760). Code today: (a) vehicle_value subtracts only 0.25 when another pilot (human or bot, same team; any player in FFA) is >= 3 m closer to the vehicle, by straight distance, no heading or speed; (b) claims exist only between bots (MA2_ORD_GET_VEHICLE; not even swaps, see the swap-claim fact); the human never holds a claim; (c) every bot picks and claims at t = 0.0 before the human has moved; (d) no count of free 'Mechs anywhere (usable, pick_vehicle, pick_swap and the pad change-ride roll all ignore humans). A bot 20 m behind the human can still out-value it (Mech 1.0 vs -0.25 penalty). Proposed (t3-sk-B03/B04, follow-up): one claim table with hard bot claims + a soft human-intent claim (closing > 2 m/s for >= 0.5 s, heading within 35 deg, within 120 m, lasting 3 s) and a last-free-'Mech reservation (free <= humans on foot -> 'Mech unusable to bots); log [BOT-YIELD] / [BOT-RESERVE]; proof plan = rerun custfull2_td (before 33/41) and extend RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_BOARD with a kind.
facts.how_to_use: Bots audit t3-sk-B01.B05.

facts.title: Measured per skill in 6v6 CTF runs: damage per bot-minute is flat (985 / 947 / 1037 / 1007), the goal mix is the same, dodging is the only clearly skill-scaled behaviour

subject.id: bots-t3d skill-counts.md (ctf_recruit / ctf / ctf_veteran / ctf_elite / ctf_mixed .log)

facts.fact: Game runs: damage per bot-minute Recruit 985 / Regular 947 / Veteran 1037 / Elite 1007; shots per minute 74 / 73 / 100 / 97; kills 63 / 51 / 84 / 91 (so kills rise, damage does not); goal mix the same at every skill (swap 24-27 %, objective 24-31 %, attack 18-29 %); dodging is the only clearly skill-scaled behaviour (0.23 / 0.36 / 1.19 / 2.30 per minute); peek-hide 0.03-0.07 per minute and cover 0-2 % at every skill; time in a 'Mech Elite 22 % vs Regular 28 % (any vehicle 27 % vs 34 %), time dead (goal=none) Elite 12 % vs Regular 8 %, swap churn ~24 % of Elite time; friendly-fire holds 154-350 per bot-minute at every skill (Regular lowest). The lower Elite end damage in these runs is explained by less time in a 'Mech and more swap/dead time, not by peek/hide. Flag grabs 0/1/1/0, captures 0. Mixed run (--skill 4, small samples) consistent. Skill spread in CTF itself is not re-measured yet. See bots3-6v6-td-on-the-editor-fresh-map-skill-ladder-holds-elite-7-kills-1-death-vs-recruit-1-2-attack-samples-8-45-47-percent.

facts.title: The human player's pilot body has no campaign AI, so the bot-side drive helpers cannot move it; tests that need the human to walk must use MCP game_key / game_mouse
facts.fact: Code + game: the human player's pilot body has no campaign AI (vcall actor+0x200 returns none), so the bot-side drive helpers (MoveTo via AI, body_walk_direct, the body speed/turn calls) do not move it. RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_BOARD's walk therefore never moved the human in 3 runs ([HUMAN-HP] pos constant); it was also VTOL-only (ma2_bots_core.c:3734-3760). Consequence: any bots test that needs the human to move (the 'race for a Mech' case, yield rule A/B) must drive the human through the MCP tools game_key / game_mouse: camera-relative WASD, about 30 degrees per 800 px of mouse movement at sensitivity 100, Y = Q (enter/exit).
facts.how_to_use: follow-up test design (t3-sk-B05 proof plan); do not extend RECOMP_TEST_HUMAN_BOARD with a 'Mech kind expecting it to move the human.

facts.title: Base War's objectives are MARoot objective slots 0 and 1 that name the power plants BY UID; the editor's kit copy left them dangling, so the match ended ~5 s in ('Blue Team Wins!')

subject.id: MARoot ObjectiveType0/1, NumObjectiveObjects0/1, ob0obj0 / ob1obj0; MABuilding sub_00127ED7 / sub_00128000

facts.fact: Code + file read: the game's Base War objectives are MARoot objective slots 0 and 1 (ObjectiveType0/1 = 9 Red base / 10 Blue base, NumObjectiveObjects0/1 = 1), and each slot names its target BY UID: retail BoggedDown ob0obj0 = 126031 (BldInd_BW_PowerPlant_Red), ob1obj0 = 124373 (BldInd_BW_PowerPlant_Blue). On the editor map t3d_allmodes the plants had been renumbered by the kit clone (players.cpp clone_from_world gives clones new UIDs and remaps refs only INSIDE the clone; MARoot is not in the clone) to 139757 / 139759, and in multiplayer saves the step that rewrites ob%dobj%d from the MAObjectiveType parents (triggers.cpp compile_expanded, the 'ri >= 0 && !s.multiplayer' block ~line 557) is skipped, so slots 0 and 1 kept the retail UIDs, which point at nothing. The game then treats Red's base objective (slot 0) as already gone and Blue wins at once: 'Blue Team Wins!' with every Blue player on 1 point at t = 3 ([OBJ-PL] stats word 18 = 1 for all nat = 2 players, basewar.log). MABuilding sub_00127ED7 / sub_00128000 (recomp_0029.c ~3970-3990) read MARoot objective record [ObjectiveNumber].type (table 0x50E860 + n * 0x64 + 0x10) and set building+0x1E4 = 1 when it is 9 or 10 (= Base War plant); that part still works on editor maps because the MAObjectiveType under each plant keeps ObjectiveNumber 0/1. The per-frame Base War win check itself was not traced. Second difference (probably not the cause): the three retail MoeEntitySets ('Invulnerabilty at Start' = the 4 VTOL bays, 'Red Stuff' 15 members, 'Blue Stuff' 14) are EMPTY on every editor-made map, so root trigger 'TT - Setup' actions (MAActionNation on Red/Blue Stuff, MAActionAttribute Modifier 3 on Invulnerabilty) hit nothing. Side note: on the editor map the bay vehicles' MAOwnerController MoverTemplateUID does not resolve in world.wdf (it does in retail). Game proof pending: vs the control f20_boggeddown_copy.ma2map. GAME PROOF: with the 91d5795 objective-slot fix the editor map no longer ends at ~5 s; both plants take steady damage, Red 24000 -> 13785 (57%), Blue 24000 -> 15691 (65%); [C7] basewar t=180 dmg_red=8574 dmg_blue=7484. So the dangling-UID cause is confirmed (fixed map runs, control ended at once). See base-war-bogged-down-2000hp-targets-are-indestructible-vtol-bays-plants-are-the-24000hp-ones.
facts.how_to_use: Editor MP authoring (kit clones): any object a MARoot key names by UID must be remapped; Check should flag a Base War map whose objective slots point at missing UIDs. Verified in game 2026-10-27: maps re-saved with editor 91d5795 or later run Base War normally.

Right-lane trip ends: A paused(fight) 5, retarget 4, stalled 5; B paused 13, retarget 13, stalled 2. No bot reached the apex in either run. Not merged. LANEBACK PROVEN + MERGED: flank lanes are also planned BACK from the lane_b spawn, so the east team walks its own polylines (side 9 = none that way). Ledge detail: the +1 lane's east end is a ledge (y 11-17 at 1328-1338,636-656) over the east spawn, so planned west -> east it drops at lane points 13.18; planned east -> west with the centre / left made expensive, the planner finds its own +1 route (apex 816,512) and east bots do reach it. Proof rl4 (rightlane4.exe = 24597e3, NRC 5v6 240 s, 0 faults, bots-t3a\rl4.log.gz): east team within 250 m of the +1 apex 708,542: 93 samples / 2 bots (rl3: 0); west 77 / 2 (rl3: 0); share_right 146 (rl3 78), fight_right 112 (32), share_left 199 (95), share_centre 503 (733); back_found 2. The merge itself was not re-smoked. Switch RECOMP_BOT_LANE_BACK=0 / [Bots] LaneBack=0. facts.title: On-foot pilot weapon = the PILOT BOMB, not a gun: the gun-fire path (sub_18482E -> sub_F13E9) refuses a pilot because no gun mount exists on a pilot body; the left mouse on foot goes through the DropPack bomb path instead
facts.fact: A g3 diag run (fresh-map Not It, [BOT-PFIRE] with sub_18482E gate fields, t3-modes 886e0ea) is queued. Retail Not It is unaffected because bots there start in Battle Armor and fire from vehicles. PFIRE NARROWED: the selected weapon slot matches (w+0x98 = arsenal+0x7C = 0), actor bit 17 is clear, and the refire timer ai+0x118 is a clock stamp (clock ~48000; clearing it makes the game re-arm +5 s, still returns 0), so it is NOT the sub_1858EF ready check. The refusal is inside the weapon's own fire sub_12B234 -> sub_F13E9, which returns al=0 when the mount object w+0x9C does not resolve from the slot ids w+0x84.0x90, or when mount+0x13C == 0; otherwise it calls sub_CFE30. A diag build printing those fields (same line for Mech/BA bots) is ready; g3 run queued. ROOT CAUSE GAME-PROVEN: every bot pilot's pistol has mount slots 0,-1,-1,-1 and its mount object w+0x9C stays 0, so sub_F1364(slot id 0) resolves nothing -> the weapon's own fire sub_F13E9 returns 0 -> sub_18482E returns 0. The pistol mount lookup (decoded): slot id 0 -> owner MACorporeal tree +0xA8 must hold a MAModSubObjectState whose byte +0xBC == 0. Open: what a HUMAN pilot's pistol has at w+0x84 / w+0x9C (id -> mount via class [0x4EAF2C] lookup, x+4 -> +0xA8 -> sub_B2BE0 -> vt+0x78); likely the hand / hardpoint mount is registered only for the player-controlled pilot, or the id must be the pilot body's mount id. A PMOUNT diag (t3-modes 9f7ba34: bot pilot vs human pilot weapon mount chain) is queued on g2/g3; code-side fix work meanwhile. RESOLVED: BY DESIGN: a weapon fires only from a MOUNT = a MAModSubObjectState node (class [0x4EB01C], byte +0xBC == the weapon's slot id; slots are w+0x84.0x90, -1 = empty) in its MACorporeal owner's model tree (+0xA8). Both sub_F13E9 and sub_F1458 (via sub_F1306 -> sub_F1364) return 0 without one. The lookup is sub_B2BE0(tree, id, callback 0xF13C2, 0) -> [0x4EAF48], then the node's vt+0x78 (0x107B2B on 'Mech mounts). Control (nrc_copy): every 'Mech, human and bot, has mount ids 0 and 1. Every on-foot pilot, HUMAN INCLUDED, has none (ids 0-7 all empty), and the human pilot shows no gun in the screenshot: the arsenal pistol (class C14020DA, slots 0,-1,-1,-1) is unmounted, so in the retail game an on-foot pilot cannot shoot. This corrects the earlier 'bot-only defect' reading (but see Correction: 'cannot shoot' is true only for a GUN). Bot implication: on foot, bots should not 'engage' with fire (wasted eng_s and friendly-fire holds) but go for a vehicle / hijack / evade; Not It and LMS on maps where everyone starts on foot need vehicles on the map or a BA / 'Mech start (see the MARoot start-slot fact). Read 'pistol' here as the bomb placer and 'never fire' as 'never place a bomb'. See pilot-on-foot-weapon-is-the-pilot-bomb-not-a-pistol-remote-or-proximity-detonation-user. Behaviour vtable slot 50 = sub_1B0682 (vt 0x477410 / 0x47DF90) reads avatar+0x26C: bit 17 set (the same fire bit [BOT-PFIRE] reads) and bit 25 clear -> sub_1041FB -> DropPackManager at avatar+0x254 (vt 0x4678A8). The bomb = DropPack 'Explosive Pack' (key 5A255EC2) on every pilot template (IsDropPackEnabled 1; ArmingTime 0.1 s, ManuallyTrigger 1; body 116392 Env_Detonator_Player, blast MAEffect 125315), with MATriggerLogic + MATriggerRadius + MATriggerTimer children. Press handler sub_E664C (state +0x80 0/1/2): with a pack deployed (+0x84, pack+0x8C), state 0 and +0x7C set, a press calls sub_E6838 = detonate (second press); otherwise a press sets state 1 = place (placement/update sub_E66B5 from 0x10441C). The 'Mech-walks-over / ~5 s linger trigger is most likely the pack's trigger-radius / timer DATA (LOW: no constant found in code). Bot recipe (MEDIUM, inferred): skip sub_18482E on foot; set avatar+0x26C bit 17 (bit 25 clear) for a tick and let slot 50 run (or call sub_1041FB with ebx = avatar); first check avatar+0x254 != 0, byte behavior+0x6E4 == 0, byte +0x6BD, and whether the bot behaviour reaches slot 50 at all; press again to detonate. See wiki pilot-bomb-is-droppack-. and pilot-on-foot-weapon-is-the-pilot-bomb-. BOT BOMBS ARE LIVE: bots now plant pilot bombs through this path; see bots3-bot-pilots-plant-pilot-bombs-. for the mechanism and proof.

facts.title: MP power-up respawn: 'RespawnTime' lives on MACrateGenerator (not MAPowerupDrop); countdown ticked by vt slot 7 (0x152B98) with stamp +0x8C / interval +0x88; respawn spawns at the generator's own position (+0x78); clock restarts every frame while predicate 0x152B32 holds
facts.fact: OWNER: the 'Powerup respawner (Multiplayer only)' object is a MACrateGenerator; MAPowerupDrop children hold the powerup template (NumPowerups always 1). RespawnTime is stored at [this+0x68] (get/set 0x152A98 / save 0x152A32; the catalog says offset 136 = 0x88 and read site 0x152ABE; the copy +0x68 -> +0x88 was not found, probably ctor 0x15296A / 0x152C6C or helper 0xC4B2D). COUNTDOWN (code-confirmed): vt slot 7 (0x152B98) each tick: elapsed = now - stamp [this+0x8C] compared with interval [this+0x88]; on expiry restamp, pick a child (0x152AFA), spawn it with 0x17E701 at [this+0x78] (the generator's own position vector) => V2 SAME SPOT: yes (code-confirmed for the argument; 'the call spawns the entity' is inferred). Slot 11 (0x152A14) writes the stamp only when predicate 0x0C364B holds. V1: the clock probably does NOT start at level start; it starts when slot 11 sees the child taken (inferred pickup path), and while predicate 0x152B32 holds the tick re-stamps every frame, so it counts only while the spot is clear (inferred; needs an in-game trace of slot 11 and 0x152B32). The tick is gated by a global byte [0x18F10 object +0x69]; no per-crate active flag found. Taken power-ups park at the map edge (1,1 / 300,0) while waiting (older wiki fact, not rechecked). The same MACrateGenerator class is used for vehicle entry zones, so RespawnTime also sits on that role. UNKNOWN: predicates 0x0B3BA0 (taken check), 0x152B32 (occupancy scan, radius), who calls slot 11 (the real pickup hook). In-game test: set RespawnTime 5 s, pick up, time the return, stand on the spot, log 0x152B32.
facts.how_to_use: For a power-up-timing trick read the interval from the generator ([this+0x68]/[+0x88]) and the stamp [+0x8C]; confirm the pickup hook in game before relying on a countdown estimate.
